title: Advanced Reactivity: ref, reactive, and Beyond
description: Master `ref`, `reactive`, `shallowRef`, `readonly`, and when to use each.

slides.title: ref vs reactive
slides.content:
# ref

- Wraps a value (primitive or object) into a reactive **ref** object with a `.value` property.
- Use `ref` for primitives or when you want to pass a single reactive variable.

# reactive

- Makes an object deeply reactive.
- Only works for objects (including arrays).
- Cannot be directly used for primitives.

```javascript
import { ref, reactive } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0);       // count.value
const state = reactive({    // state.count
  count: 0
});
```

In templates, `ref` automatically unwraps when used as a top‑level property.

slides.title: Shallow & Readonly Variants
slides.content:
# shallowRef / shallowReactive

- `shallowRef` – only the `.value` assignment is reactive; nested properties are not.
- `shallowReactive` – only the first‑level properties are reactive; deeper properties are not.

Useful for large objects where you don't need deep reactivity, improving performance.

# readonly / shallowReadonly

- `readonly` – makes an object deeply readonly (cannot be mutated).
- `shallowReadonly` – only first‑level are readonly.

```javascript
const original = reactive({ count: 0, nested: { num: 1 } });
const copy = readonly(original);
copy.count = 1; // warning in console
```

slides.title: Choosing the Right API
slides.content:
| Use Case | Recommended |
|----------|-------------|
| Primitive value (string, number, boolean) | `ref` |
| Object that will be mutated deeply | `reactive` |
| Object that will be reassigned often | `ref` (and use `.value` when reassigning) |
| Large object where only top‑level changes matter | `shallowReactive` |
| Expose reactive data without allowing mutations | `readonly` |

quizData.question: What is the main difference between `ref` and `reactive` in Vue 3?

options.text: `ref` is for primitive values; `reactive` is for objects
`ref` creates a wrapper with `.value`; `reactive` directly proxies the object

quizData.explanation: `ref` returns a reactive wrapper object with a `.value` property, while `reactive` directly makes the object reactive without a wrapper.
